definition: Math benchmarks: grade-school word problems (GSM8K) and competition problems (MATH).
details: Math benchmarks: grade-school word problems (GSM8K) and competition problems (MATH). Historically the proving grounds for chain-of-thought and reasoning RL; both are near-saturated for frontier reasoning models, pushing evaluation toward harder sets (AIME-level and beyond).

explainer.lead: MATH and GSM8K are the benchmark pair that made chain-of-thought measurable, and they set the agenda for reasoning training. They matter now mainly as a baseline: frontier reasoning models have nearly saturated them.

tiers.eli5: These are sets of maths test questions — primary-school word problems and hard competition problems — used to score how well a computer can do sums and puzzles.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers report GSM8K and MATH scores to show reasoning gains from chain-of-thought or reasoning RL. The pitfall is treating a high MATH score as broad reasoning ability once the benchmark is saturated.
tiers.paperLevel: Accuracy on GSM8K (grade-school word problems) and MATH (competition problems), scored against gold answers. Both are near-saturated for frontier reasoning models, so evaluation is shifting to AIME-level and harder sets.

explainer.example: A model trained with reasoning RL moves from around 50% to over 90% on GSM8K; the team then reports AIME-level results because MATH no longer separates models.
